notes: Values are typed. Installed vs equipment-only, AC vs DC, per-kW_H2 vs per-kW_e and nominal vs real price bases are kept in separate fields deliberately; do not merge them. 'evidence_strength' is one of strong / moderate / weak / none.

claims.meaning: Specific electricity consumption of the brief's reference electrolyser module
claims.scope: AC power, full system (water purification + PEM stack + balance of plant), beginning of life, ITM POSEIDON 20 MW module
claims.recommended_baseline: Use 55.9 kWh/kg as the single AC conversion; apply no additional rectifier/transformer loss and no separate water-treatment energy term

sensitivity_range.basis: 55.9 for 20/50 MW modules; 57.0 measured for the 2 MW NEPTUNE II; higher values represent degradation, which the data sheet does not quantify

claims.meaning: Boundary of the 55.9 kWh/kg figure
claims.value: Full system AC consumption at beginning of life; excludes H2 compression above 31 bar(g) and excludes any degradation allowance
claims.scope: ITM POSEIDON data sheet footnote
claims.recommended_baseline: State the boundary in the run manifest; treat compression above 31 bar(g) as a separate costed module

claims.meaning: Minimum operating load of the reference module when running
claims.scope: POSEIDON 20 MW; footnoted as arising from 4 pairs turned down to 25% applied load, i.e. a module-configuration property, not a physical PEM limit
claims.recommended_baseline: Keep 20% for the reference module, with a binary on/off variable so that 0 output is distinct from 20% output

sensitivity_range.basis: 12.5% on ITM ALPHA 50 (S2 p2); 25% on ITM NEPTUNE II 2 MW (S3 p2); alternative module choices move the floor

claims.meaning: Maximum load / ramp behaviour
claims.unit: % of installed capacity (max); 10%/s ramp up, 50%/s ramp down
claims.scope: All three ITM modules
claims.source_ref: S1 p2; S2 p2; S3 p2
claims.recommended_baseline: Ramping is non-binding at daily resolution; do not model intraday ramping in the Tier1 daily model

claims.meaning: Hydrogen production rate per MW of electrolyser at full load
claims.unit: kg H2 per hour per MW_e
claims.scope: Derived: 1000 kWh/h / 55.9 kWh/kg
claims.recommended_baseline: 429 kg/day and 156.7 t/yr per MW_e at 98% availability; use for capacity-to-kg balance checks

claims.meaning: Hydrogen delivery pressure at the electrolyser outlet
claims.scope: POSEIDON 20 MW (ALPHA 50 and NEPTUNE II: 30 bar(g))
claims.source_ref: S1 p2; S2 p2; S3 p2
claims.recommended_baseline: Value H2 at the plant gate at 30-31 bar(g); any further compression is a separate costed module

claims.meaning: Discrete commercial module sizes available for the capacity decision
claims.scope: ITM NEPTUNE II (2 MW), POSEIDON (20 MW), ALPHA 50 (50 MW); a 5 MW NEPTUNE is advertised but its data sheet was not read
claims.source_ref: S1 p1-2; S2 p2; S3 p2; ITM product index
claims.recommended_baseline: Capacity = integer count of {2, 20, 50} MW modules, with a finite maximum count; do not use a continuous capacity variable

claims.meaning: Electrolyser CAPEX, equipment / full-scope plant list price
claims.scope: ITM ALPHA 50 list price EUR 50,000,000 for 50 MW; scope includes stacks, PSU incl. MV transformer and rectifier, water purification/polishing, cooling, H2 purification, DCS and ISBL piping; excludes civils, installation, grid-connection reinforcement and compression above 30 bar(g)
claims.recommended_baseline: Lower bound of the CAPEX range; convert at a stated FX rate (0.85 EUR/GBP gives about GBP 0.85 m/MW_e)

sensitivity_range.basis: FX 0.80-0.92 EUR/GBP; list price is not a negotiated or audited transaction price

claims.meaning: Electrolyser CAPEX, installed nth-of-a-kind cost (government cost evidence)
claims.scope: PEM, 10 MW reference plant, 2020 commissioning, medium case; scope covers stack, balance of plant (drier, cooling, de-ox), civil works and electricity grid connection; excludes H2 compression. Converted from GBP 1158.63/kW H2 HHV by dividing by the paired electrical efficiency 1.397
claims.source_ref: S10 sheet 'Technical and cost assumptions' rows 3,10-16; S8 p16 for cost scope
claims.recommended_baseline: Central engineering anchor; uprate for price year before use

sensitivity_range.basis: table low/high CAPEX pairs divided by their paired efficiencies (953.59/1.2319; 1887.51/1.6256), all 2020 real prices

claims.meaning: Electrolyser CAPEX, 2025 projection in the same government evidence
claims.scope: PEM, 10 MW, 2025 commissioning, medium case (730.29 GBP/kW H2 HHV, efficiency 1.3208); same cost scope as R3-09
claims.source_ref: S10 sheet 'Technical and cost assumptions' rows 3,10-16
claims.recommended_baseline: Use only if the model adopts the source's own cost-reduction projection; not a market observation

claims.meaning: CAPEX unit trap: government electrolyser CAPEX is quoted per kW of hydrogen output (HHV), not per kW of electricity input
claims.value: GBP/kW H2 HHV divided by (kWh_e per kWh H2 HHV) gives GBP/kW_e; the factor is about 1.4
claims.scope: BEIS/DESNZ 2021 annex
claims.recommended_baseline: Always convert to kW_e before putting an electrolyser CAPEX into an optimiser; using the table value directly understates CAPEX by about 28%

claims.meaning: Electrolyser CAPEX, committed whole-project capital per MW (first-of-a-kind, UK)
claims.scope: HAR1: GBP 413 m private capital across 125 MW of small (5.2-24.5 MW) FOAK projects; includes bespoke civils, connection works, compression/storage and developer margin. Adding the >GBP 90 m Net Zero Hydrogen Fund grant gives about GBP 4.02 m/MW gross
claims.recommended_baseline: Upper bound of the CAPEX range; describes what UK FOAK projects actually committed, not a repeat-build cost

sensitivity_range.basis: grant treatment (private-only vs gross) and expected FOAK-to-NOAK cost reduction

claims.meaning: Recommended bounded electrolyser CAPEX set for the optimiser (installed, per MW_e)
claims.scope: Low = ITM list equipment price; core = BEIS 2020 central GBP 0.83 m/MW_e uprated by an assumed factor 1.25; high = HAR1 committed project capital
claims.recommended_baseline: Core GBP 1.5 m/MW_e, with the full range reported; the 1.25 uprating is an assumption pending R4/F-01 deflator work

sensitivity_range.basis: 3.9x swing; the single largest driver of the electrolyser investment decision after the H2 value

claims.meaning: Fixed operating expenditure of the electrolyser
claims.scope: PEM medium case, 2020 commissioning, 10 MW; converted from GBP 36.72/kW H2 HHV per year by dividing by 1.397
claims.recommended_baseline: About 1.75%/yr of the core CAPEX; carry as a fixed annual charge, and absorb unevidenced water cost here rather than inventing a GBP/m3 figure

sensitivity_range.basis: table low/high rows divided by paired efficiencies (32.38/1.397; 42.73/1.397)

claims.meaning: Variable operating expenditure of the electrolyser
claims.scope: PEM medium 2020: GBP 0.0039/kWh H2 HHV multiplied by 39.4 kWh/kg
claims.source_ref: S10 row 24-26; S5 p10 for the 39.4 conversion
claims.recommended_baseline: Apply per kg produced, in addition to the electricity cost

sensitivity_range.basis: table low 0.0029 and high 0.0089 GBP/kWh H2 HHV, times 39.4

claims.meaning: Stack replacement share of plant CAPEX and cycle interval (PEM)
claims.scope: PEM; capitalised into the levelised cost over a 30-year technology life (alkaline 50%/9 yr, SOE 60%/7 yr)
claims.recommended_baseline: Model as a cash outflow of 60% of electrolyser CAPEX at years 11 and 22, not as a silent OPEX uplift

sensitivity_range.basis: stack share differs by technology; interval could lengthen with stack life improvements

claims.meaning: Electrolyser plant economic life and hurdle rate used in the government cost evidence
claims.scope: BEIS/DESNZ 2021 annex, all electrolysis technologies
claims.recommended_baseline: Use 30 years and 10% for comparability with the CAPEX sources; R4/F-01 owns the final discount convention

claims.meaning: HAR1 weighted average hydrogen strike price (nominal as-paid basis)
claims.price_year: nominal (2023 award; paid over the contract term)
claims.scope: 11 successful HAR1 projects, 125 MW, weighted by lifetime hydrogen volumes; Low Carbon Hydrogen Agreement, 15-year support; subsidy varies with the natural gas reference price
claims.recommended_baseline: Use only as a policy-supported value scenario, never as a market price or as revenue available without an LCHA

sensitivity_range.basis: same settlement expressed in 2012 prices (GBP 175/MWh) versus nominal

claims.meaning: Hydrogen energy content used to convert GBP/MWh to GBP/kg
claims.scope: Higher Heating Value basis; the same report gives LHV = 33.33 kWh/kg
claims.source_ref: S5 p10; S6 Table A1 p36
claims.recommended_baseline: Use 39.4 for GBP/MWh(HHV)-to-GBP/kg conversions and 33.33 if an LHV-based price is quoted; never use either as the electrolyser electricity input (that is 55.9)

claims.meaning: Verification of the brief's GBP 9.5/kg derivation
claims.scope: 241 GBP/MWh x 39.4 kWh/kg / 1000 = 9.4954; arithmetic confirmed. It values hydrogen energy content at the HAR1 strike price, not the production cost
claims.recommended_baseline: Adopt GBP 9.50/kg as the core supported-value scenario, labelled nominal and LCHA-conditional

claims.meaning: Same supported value expressed in the real basis used by the source
claims.scope: 175 GBP/MWh (2012 prices) x 39.4 kWh/kg / 1000
claims.recommended_baseline: Report alongside the nominal figure; use this if the model runs in constant 2012 prices

claims.meaning: Recommended hydrogen value ladder for sensitivity analysis
claims.scope: Low = lecturer's spoken illustration in the launch transcript, not a market observation; core = HAR1 supported value; high = unsourced stress case
claims.source_ref: S11 (transcript TC-05) for the low case; S4 for the core; none for the high
claims.recommended_baseline: Core GBP 9.5/kg for the headline case; the high case must be labelled as having no source and must not be presented as evidence

sensitivity_range.basis: at GBP 2.50/kg the electrolyser loses about GBP 3/kg on electricity alone, so the investment case exists only at supported values

claims.meaning: Hydrogen revenue per unit of electricity consumed (break-even price of forgone electricity)
claims.unit: GBP per MWh of electricity input
claims.scope: 9.50 GBP/kg divided by 55.9 kWh/kg, before electrolyser CAPEX and OPEX
claims.recommended_baseline: The H2 route beats direct electricity sale only while the forgone electricity is worth less than about GBP 170/MWh; including CAPEX and OPEX the break-even falls to about GBP 140/MWh

sensitivity_range.basis: 55.9-64 kWh/kg specific consumption and GBP 9.5-12/kg hydrogen value

claims.meaning: Guaranteed commercial offtake price and volume for a producer outside HAR1
claims.unit: GBP per kg; tonnes per day
claims.scope: Searched: DESNZ publications via the gov.uk search API, ITM Power product pages and data sheets. No public firm merchant offtake price or volume for a Scottish producer was obtained
claims.recommended_baseline: Carry hydrogen price and offtake cap as explicit scenario parameters; the model must not assume unlimited offtake at a fixed price

sensitivity_range.basis: offtake cap scenarios of 0 / 5 / 20 t per day are suggested for illustration only; none is evidence-based

claims.meaning: Levelised cost of hydrogen storage by technology (total, and conversion/compression share)
claims.scope: Levelised storage cost, cycle rates as listed; underlying source DNV via the DESNZ report footnote
claims.source_ref: S6 Table A2 p36; S5 p21
claims.recommended_baseline: Optional module only. Salt cavern is the cheapest but needs 9 cycles/yr; a 700 bar vessel costs about GBP 1.39/kg levelised

sensitivity_range.basis: technology choice; aquifer and depleted-field estimates are more uncertain at scale

claims.meaning: Levelised cost of hydrogen transport
claims.unit: GBP per kg H2 per 100 km
claims.scope: Levelised transport cost for a stated distance; the report itself warns that distance is often unstated in the literature
claims.source_ref: S7 Table A4 p38; S5 p21 and p29
claims.recommended_baseline: Optional module only, and only with an explicit distance. Pipeline is 8-10x cheaper per kg than road trailer

claims.meaning: Reconversion (hydrogen back to electricity) equipment cost and efficiency
claims.value: No equipment cost or efficiency data obtained
claims.scope: Not researched to conclusion in this pass; the brief treats reconversion as optional and BL-08 keeps it outside the direct-sale baseline
claims.recommended_baseline: Do not include reconversion in the baseline. If added, enforce a physical ceiling: 39.4 kWh/kg (HHV) x efficiency against 55.9 kWh/kg input, i.e. about 42% round-trip at 60% conversion efficiency

sensitivity_range.basis: round-trip at 50-64% reconversion efficiency; any value near 100% implies energy creation

claims.meaning: Thermal basis conflict when reconverting: LHV vs HHV energy content
claims.scope: The DESNZ report uses HHV for its own conversions but tabulates LHV = 33.33 kWh/kg in Table A1
claims.source_ref: S5 p10; S6 Table A1 p36
claims.recommended_baseline: Fix one thermal basis across value, reconversion and reporting, and state it; mixing them creates a silent 18% discrepancy (39.4/33.33)

claims.meaning: Conditions that would make electrolyser capacity unbounded in the optimisation
value: unlimited offtake at a fixed price
unlimited electricity import at a fixed price below the implied GBP 170/MWh
39.4 kWh/kg used as the input consumption
reconversion efficiency at or above unity
free H2 storage with no losses or capacity limit
claims.scope: Modelling integrity checks
claims.recommended_baseline: Assert a finite offtake cap, a finite import cap from R1, a discrete module grid, a binary on/off at 20% load, and an energy balance that uses 55.9 kWh/kg as input and 39.4 kWh/kg only as output energy content

claims.meaning: Bounded equipment set recommended to the optimiser
claims.value: Integer counts of {2, 20, 50} MW modules up to a stated finite maximum; no bespoke or fractional capacity
claims.scope: Justified by the ITM product grid rather than an arbitrary numerical bound (M-05)
claims.recommended_baseline: Report the optimum as a module count so that it is physically orderable

claims.meaning: Water supply requirement and cost
claims.value: Potable water (ALPHA 50) or DI water post-polishing (POSEIDON); no unit cost obtained
claims.scope: Data sheets state input water quality only
claims.recommended_baseline: Absorb into the BEIS-derived fixed OPEX (which already covers BoP) and declare the assumption; do not invent a water price

claims.meaning: Electrolyser degradation rate over life
claims.value: Not quantified in the manufacturer data sheet; the 55.9 kWh/kg figure is explicitly beginning of life
claims.scope: ITM data sheets give beginning-of-life consumption only
claims.recommended_baseline: Keep beginning-of-life 55.9 with the BEIS stack-replacement schedule as the degradation proxy; do not invent an annual degradation percentage

claims.meaning: HAR1 eligibility and support mechanism, which determines whether the GBP 9.5/kg can be claimed at all
claims.value: Competitively allocated Low Carbon Hydrogen Agreement to 11 named projects totalling 125 MW; revenue support with strike adjusted against the natural gas reference price; maximum NZHF capex grant intensity 20% in this round
claims.scope: Applies to England, Scotland and Wales; does not confer any entitlement on a new or hypothetical project
claims.source_ref: S4 and the underlying publication page
claims.recommended_baseline: Treat the supported value as a scenario assumption for a scheme that holds, or could credibly hold, an LCHA; otherwise treat it as unavailable

claims.meaning: Internal consistency check between the manufacturer's specific consumption and the government cost evidence
claims.scope: BEIS PEM 2020 medium electrical efficiency 1.397 kWh_e/kWh H2 HHV multiplied by 39.4 kWh/kg, compared with ITM's 55.9 kWh/kg
claims.recommended_baseline: The two independent evidence lines agree within 2%, so pairing BEIS CAPEX with the manufacturer's 55.9 kWh/kg is coherent
